mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 1 Series M135i engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series M135i engine replacement typically costs £3,500-£8,000 for a reconditioned or rebuilt N55 unit supply-only. With supply and fit, expect £5,000-£10,000 depending on the specialist and location. Main dealer new engine quotes can exceed £12,000 for parts alone.

mainEntity.name: What engine is in the BMW M135i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW M135i (F20/F21, 2012-2016) is powered by a 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six petrol engine with the engine code N55B30. It produces 320 hp (235 kW) at 5,800 rpm and 450 Nm of torque from 1,300-4,500 rpm. The N55 features a single twin-scroll turbocharger, Valvetronic variable valve lift and direct injection.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW M135i engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - the N55 engine in the BMW M135i is generally regarded as reliable, with far fewer major failure points than the twin-turbo N54 it replaced. Common issues include oil leaks (valve cover gasket, oil filter housing gasket), Valvetronic wear, and water pump failure. Timing chain failure is incredibly rare on the N55, unlike the N47 and N20.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 1 Series M135i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series M135i engine replacement typically takes 2-4 days for a specialist to complete, including removal of the old N55 unit and fitting the replacement. The complexity of the six-cylinder turbo engine means labour time is higher than for four-cylinder models.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW M135i and M140i?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the BMW M135i and M140i are performance models of the 1 Series, but they use different engines. The M135i (2012-2016) uses the N55 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six producing 320 hp, while the M140i (2016-2019) uses the B58 3.0-litre turbocharged straight-six producing 340 hp.

mainEntity.name: Does a BMW 1 Series M135i rebuilt engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt BMW 1 Series M135i engine supplied through EnginesMarket comes with a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. This covers the engine against manufacturing defects and component failure, giving you peace of mind when investing in a replacement N55 unit.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 1 Series M135i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW M135i was launched in 2012 as the first M Performance model in the 1 Series range, sitting above the 135i and below the full-fat 1M Coupe. Powered by a 3.0-litre N55 turbocharged straight-six producing 320 hp, it combined rear-wheel-drive dynamics with genuine hot-hatch performance - 0-62 mph in 4.9 seconds (automatic) and a 155 mph limited top speed. The M135i represented BMW's answer to the Audi RS3 and Mercedes A45 AMG, offering a more engaging, rear-driven alternative. Production ran from 2012 to 2016 across the F20 (five-door) and F21 (three-door) body styles, before being replaced by the M140i with the B58 engine.

milestones.description: N55B30O0, 3.0L single twin-scroll turbo straight-six, 320 hp (235 kW), launched with the F20 five-door and F21 three-door 1 Series
8-speed automatic transmission option introduced alongside the manual
F20/F21 LCI (Life Cycle Impulse) update; M135i continues with N55 engine producing 320 hp
M135i replaced by M140i with B58 engine producing 340 hp; the M135i badge is retired

commonProblems.h2: BMW 1 Series M135i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: H3: The BMW 1 Series M135i is powered exclusively by the N55B30 engine - a 3.0-litre single twin-scroll turbocharged straight-six that produces 320 hp and 450 Nm of torque. The N55 is generally regarded as reliable, with far fewer major failure points than the twin-turbo N54 it replaced. However, like all modern BMW engines, it has its common issues - primarily oil leaks, cooling system components, and charge pipe failures. Replacement demand for the BMW M135i is lower than for four-cylinder BMWs, but when failures occur, the cost of repair can be significant. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components and a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Oil Leaks - Valve Cover, Oil Filter Housing and VANOS Solenoid Seals
problems.rootCause: The N55 engine uses gaskets and seals that can become brittle and leak over time. The valve cover gasket, oil filter housing gasket, and VANOS solenoid seals are the most common leak points. A leaking valve cover gasket can cause oil to drip onto the exhaust manifold, producing a burning smell and smoke.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve cover gasket and PCV components

repairOptions.longevity: Address oil leaks before they cause further issues
If VANOS-related fault codes are present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new gaskets and seals

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2012-2016 BMW 1 Series M135i is currently valued at approximately £8,000-£18,000 depending on mileage, condition and specification. This places the M135i firmly in the bracket where a rebuilt engine is a viable investment - replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value. For well-maintained, lower-mileage examples worth £12,000+, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with warranty is a sound investment. For cars worth under £8,000 with catastrophic engine failure, evaluate scrap value first.
problems.recommendation: The N55 is a reliable engine, and oil leaks are the most common issue. Address gasket leaks promptly - a £350-£650 specialist repair is far cheaper than dealing with the consequences of a major oil leak. If you notice white smoke or a burning smell, have the valve cover gasket inspected immediately. Unlike the N20, the N55 does not have widespread timing chain issues, making it a more dependable choice for long-term ownership.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N55B30O0 BMW 1 Series M135i engine prices

problems.h4: Valvetronic Motor & Eccentric Shaft Wear - The N55's Hidden Weakness
problems.rootCause: The N55's Valvetronic system uses a motor with a worm gear that drives the eccentric shaft. The gears can become damaged due to insufficient lubrication from extended oil change intervals or restricted oil flow. If the motor worm gear becomes damaged, the likelihood that the gears on the eccentric shaft are damaged increases. In severe cases, the eccentric shaft can wear into the cylinder head.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace Valvetronic motor and inspect eccentric shaft
repairOptions.longevity: If Valvetronic fault codes are present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace eccentric shaft and Valvetronic components
Complete rebuilt unit with new components

problems.recommendation: Valvetronic issues are usually repairable without engine replacement. A diagnostic scan will identify if fault codes are present. If Valvetronic motor failure is detected, have the eccentric shaft inspected - catching wear early can prevent a much more expensive repair. Regular oil changes with BMW-approved oil are essential to prevent Valvetronic wear.

problems.group: Electric Water Pump & Charge Pipe Failure
problems.h4: Electric Water Pump & Charge Pipe Failure
problems.rootCause: The N55 uses an electric water pump that can fail without warning. Unlike belt-driven pumps, an electric pump failure may not be preceded by a visible leak. If the pump fails, the engine can overheat rapidly. The charge pipe, which connects the intercooler to the throttle body, is known to crack under boost pressure - particularly on tuned examples.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace electric water pump and thermostat
Replace charge pipe with upgraded aluminium unit
repairOptions.longevity: If boost leak or cracked pipe detected

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new components
repairOptions.longevity: If overheating has caused significant damage

problems.recommendation: Water pump and thermostat replacement is recommended as preventative maintenance around 80,000-100,000 miles. If your M135i has not had the water pump replaced, consider doing so proactively. For the charge pipe, upgrading to an aluminium aftermarket unit is a popular and cost-effective solution that prevents future failure - especially if you're running increased boost.

finalCta.h4: Don't Let Engine Issues Write Off Your BMW 1 Series M135i
finalCta.paragraph: The N55 engine in your BMW M135i is one of BMW's most celebrated turbocharged straight-sixes - a reliable, characterful engine that deserves proper maintenance. Oil leaks, Valvetronic wear and water pump failure are the most common problems, and all are repairable without replacing the entire engine in most cases.
